name: watchface.sport_selection.item_data
evidence: Both page creation callbacks store their non-null root arguments into independent global slots, and their destroy callbacks clear them. The common row create/update functions register event code 7 with a pointer to the relevant 20-byte item as user data. The shared callback checks the returned pointer for null, then reads its item type and fields to navigate to a category or publish a chosen sport.
scope: item-data reads from the shared watchface sport/category selection callback while at least one of its pages is active
limitations: Return 0 to bypass this callback; any nonzero replacement must be a valid live item pointer with the expected 20-byte layout. Either page being open blocks installation. This does not prove shared-entry quiescence across other threads; device behavior remains unverified.
registration_evidence: The create and update row paths register the same event-7 callback with the item pointer as user data. The create path ignores the descriptor; the update function returns it to its caller.
